title: Saqsaywaman
summary: Saqsaywaman is an Inca ceremonial and military complex on the hill above Cusco, known for three tiers of zigzag walls built of enormous fitted stones. Work is placed in the mid-15th century under Pachacuti or his son, and the Spanish later took it during the siege of Cusco.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia says begun in the mid-15th century under Pachacuti (1438-1471) or possibly his son; the Peruvian inventory gives no date. End is the present: the walls and terraces stand.

where.modern_name: Parque Arqueologico Nacional de Saqsaywaman, Cusco, Peru
where.historical_name: Saqsaywaman, Inca fortress and temple complex above Cusco, Tawantinsuyu

importance.justification: Cusco's great Inca stone complex and the site of the Spanish assault in the 1536 siege.

related.because: World History Encyclopedia says work began under Pachacuti or possibly his son.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the start year (mid-15th century is one source; the Peruvian register is undated). No model written: the sources conflict on wall height (18 m in one, 5 m stones in the other) and I found no wall height from a heritage body, so the linear wall model is left out.
